name: Hierarchical Implicit Blob Cloud Model
definition: A model for representing cumulus cloud shape using a hierarchy of quasi-spherical particles (blobs). Each particle defines an implicit surface that deforms under the influence of neighbors to create furrows while maintaining continuity. The hierarchy is built recursively, with each level placed on the surface of the previous level.
summary: The Hierarchical Implicit Blob Cloud Model generates realistic cumulus clouds by recursively layering quasi-spherical particles to extract isosurfaces, distinguishing itself from explicit tessellation approaches.
